label: Sarda goat

names.text: "Capra sarda" is from the article's Italian interlanguage link, read on WebFetch; the English article gives no other alternative names.

about.text: An ancient Italian goat breed indigenous to Sardinia and raised across the island, mainly in the provinces of Cagliari and Nuoro. It is kept for its milk, which goes into local cheeses and fermented milk products, and its kids are slaughtered for meat.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: indigenous to Sardinia, raised throughout the island, particularly Cagliari and Nuoro; milk products gioddu, casu axeddu and ricotta; kids slaughtered at 7 to 10 kg.

origin.place: Sardinia, Italy. The article calls it an ancient Italian breed influenced by the Maltese goat; it gives no formation dates.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the island and provinces, and the Maltese influence. No formation dates are given, so none are used.

Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "End of 2013: 11,121 registered", citing the Associazione Nazionale della Pastorizia's 2013 provincial figures for the breed. This is the registered count, not a total; the archived registry page was not opened.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: its milk is the basis of local cheeses and fermented products; kids are slaughtered at 7 to 10 kg.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "an average of 3.94% milk protein". No year or method is given; the article's own source is not checked.

Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the FAO's 2007 listing as "not at risk", and the current DAD-IS listing as "at risk/vulnerable". The DAD-IS page itself was not opened, and the article gives no year for the current listing.

facts.v: Per lactation of 220 to 240 days, nannies average 173 litres as first-lactation, 215 litres as second, and 237 litres at later lactations (litres, not converted to kg).

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch, citing Noe et al. (2005), archived at istitutospallanzani.it. The Noe paper was not opened, so the figures are as the article gives them.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "The herdbook was established in 1981."

gaps: No world or FAOSTAT population figure; no formation date; no kg yield (the source gives litres); the 1998 population of 260,000 (with 6,577 in the herdbook) is in the article but not used, since its source is a book with no URL; the current DAD-IS risk year is not given. The item's parent was given as sheep, but the breed is a goat, so it is written under goat.
